nodes.label: Catálogo, pedido, ledger, entrega e payout
ADR-001 Modular Monolith with Specialized Processes
nodes.rationale: Local transactions preserve critical invariants while domain boundaries and three deployable processes retain future extraction points.

nodes.label: ADR-002 PostgreSQL Outbox Inbox and Explicit Concurrency
nodes.rationale: Atomic outbox and inbox transactions prevent dual-write loss and make at-least-once delivery safe through idempotency and explicit locking.

nodes.label: ADR-003 User SellerAccount and SellerMembership
nodes.rationale: Global identity, commercial tenant and authorization membership remain separate to prevent IDOR and cross-tenant leakage.

nodes.label: ADR-004 PSP Ledger Hold Transfer and Payout Responsibilities
nodes.rationale: The PSP is authoritative for external movement while an append-only balanced ledger explains internal obligations without creating a wallet.

nodes.label: ADR-005 Late Settlement Enters PAYMENT_QUARANTINED
nodes.rationale: Late settlement must not reveal delivery or sell the same unit twice before safe reassociation or idempotent refund.

nodes.label: ADR-006 Refund Request Attempt Effect Separation
nodes.rationale: Human workflow, external attempts, PSP refund, ledger effect, ticket and dispute require distinct lifecycle and audit records.

nodes.label: ADR-007 Pragmatic CQRS with Rebuildable Read Models
nodes.rationale: Optimized projections may be eventually consistent but sensitive commands always re-read and reauthorize canonical write models.

nodes.label: ADR-008 Multi-Tenant Growth Freshness RLS and Safe Drill-Down
nodes.rationale: Tenant-scoped, deduplicated projections with freshness and RLS prevent analytics from becoming a cross-tenant data leak or command authority.

nodes.label: ADR-009 Contextual Authorization SoD Step-Up and Audit
nodes.rationale: Sensitive operations require deny-by-default contextual policy, separation of duties, recent authentication and append-only audit.

nodes.label: ADR-010 REST v1 Idempotency and Problem Details
nodes.rationale: Uniform REST, problem details, optimistic concurrency and durable idempotency make retries and asynchronous recovery predictable.

nodes.label: ADR-011 Correlated Observability Controlled Replay and Tested DR
nodes.rationale: Correlation, privileged replay, reconciliation and tested restore are required to prove recovery across asynchronous financial flows.

nodes.label: ADR-012 Versioned Contracts and Documentation Gates
nodes.rationale: OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, schemas, migrations, ADRs and traceability evolve together and block orphan or incompatible changes.

nodes.label: ADR-013 Async Versioned Reviewed 2D-to-3D Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Untrusted and non-deterministic 3D generation requires isolated asynchronous processing, immutable artifacts, technical validation and human review.

nodes.label: ADR-014 Payment Resolution 168h Hold and Evidenced Manual Payout
nodes.rationale: Manual financial operations converge on canonical settlement and require provider capability, maker-checker controls, evidence and reconciliation.

nodes.label: ADR-015 Versioned Reputation Progression and Leaderboard Projections
nodes.rationale: Reviews and progression remain explainable and rebuildable through immutable contributions, compensations and versioned policies.

nodes.label: ADR-016 Consent and Capabilities Govern Omnichannel Post-Sale
nodes.rationale: Protected contact data, purpose-specific consent, suppression and official channel capabilities precede every promotional dispatch.

nodes.label: ADR-017 Studio Reuses Catalog and Listing
nodes.rationale: Studio reuses canonical catalog and listing identities; submissions stay private until reviewed and never become a parallel product.

nodes.label: ADR-018 Versioned Listing Commercial Plan Snapshot
nodes.rationale: Fees, priority and bonuses are published policy snapshots and cannot retroactively reprice orders or buy a favorable decision.

nodes.label: ADR-019 Market SEO and Crawl from Canonical Publication
nodes.rationale: Public HTML, canonical metadata, structured data and crawler policies derive from real published state and market capability.
